issue: Can a federal district court substitute the Crime Victims Fund as the payee of a restitution order after the judgment has become final, when the named victim has died?

sides.position: Substituting the Crime Victims Fund as restitution payee is permissible in some circumstances.
cases: United States v. Johnson, 378 F.3d 230 (2d Cir. 2004)
United States v. Hankins, 858 F.3d 1273 (9th Cir. 2017)

sides.position: Substituting the Crime Victims Fund as restitution payee is not permissible.
cases: United States v. Pawlinski, 374 F.3d 536 (7th Cir. 2004)
United States v. Speakman, 594 F.3d 1165 (10th Cir. 2010)

quote: We take no position on if or when it is appropriate to substitute the Crime Victims Fund as the payee, which is currently the subject of a circuit split.
cite: United States v. John Jerome O'Hara, No. 23-5720 (6th Cir. 2024)
